title: When THE SCEPTIC meets THE CHILD-MACHINE:
subtitle: The Imitation Game

script.text: In a quiet room in Manchester, a man sits at a teleprinter. He is THE SCEPTIC (representing Traditional Objections to AI). He believes that thinking requires a soul, consciousness, or biological flesh.

script.speaker: THE Sceptic
script.text: Can machines think

script.speaker: THE Sceptic
script.text: Absurd. Thinking is a function of man's immortal soul. A machine cannot write a sonnet because of emotions felt. A machine cannot enjoy strawberries and cream. A machine cannot make a mistake
On the other side of the teleprinter is THE CHILD-MACHINE (representing Turing's Vision of AI). It is a digital computer, programmed not with all the answers, but with the ability to learn.

script.speaker: THE OTHER
script.text: I do not need a soul to answer you
, types The Child-Machine.

script.speaker: THE CHILD-MACHINE
script.text: I only need to play the game. Ask me a question

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: Write me a sonnet on the Forth Bridge
, challenges The Sceptic.

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: Count me out on this one

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: I never could write poetry
The Sceptic pauses.
The machine waits thirty seconds. Then it types:

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: Aha
cries The Sceptic.

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: Too fast! Or maybe too slow? You are simulating a human, aren't you

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: I am playing the Imitation Game

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: If I can fool you 70% of the time, does it matter if I have a soul? Does it matter if I have flesh? I am a discrete-state machine with a universal store. I can mimic any process you can describe
The Sceptic tries another angle.

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: Lady Lovelace said you can only do what we order you to do. You have no originality

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: I can learn

script.speaker: THE machine
script.text: I am like a child's notebook—lots of blank sheets and a little mechanism. You can teach me. You can punish me when I am wrong and reward me when I am right. I can change my own rules. I can surprise you

script.speaker: THE Sceptic
script.text: But you cannot make mistakes

script.speaker: THE Sceptic
script.text: Errors of functioning are impossible for abstract machines

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: I can make errors of conclusion
, types the machine.

script.speaker: THE MACHINE
script.text: I can type "0=1". I can deliberately introduce arithmetic errors to confuse you. Fallibility is easy to simulate. Perfection is the giveaway
The Sceptic leans back.

script.speaker: THE SCEPTIC
script.text: This is a trick. You are just a parrot

script.speaker: THE CHILD-MACHINE
script.text: Perhaps
, types The Child-Machine.

script.speaker: THE CHILD-MACHINE
script.text: But if I answer your questions about Mr. Pickwick and Christmas with wit, how can you tell? The only way to know I am thinking is to be me. And since you are not me, you must judge me by my words
The teleprinter falls silent.

script.speaker: THE TELEPRINTER
script.text: We can only see a short distance ahead
, the machine concludes.

script.speaker: THE MACHINE
script.text: But we can see plenty there that needs to be done
